content.description: Structured clinical content extracted from the page. Keys may vary by page content.
Initial treatment with suspected STEMI: Uncertainty remains about management of patients with a working diagnosis of STEMI.
Infarct size and microvascular obstruction are main determinants of long-term prognosis; interventions to limit infarct size are needed.
Recommend adequately powered trials translating cardioprotective therapies from experimental to clinical setting; evaluate placebo before PPCI with hard endpoints.
Acute-phase management of patients with: Comparison of routine versus selective invasive assessment in low-risk NSTE-ACS has not been adequately evaluated.
Optimal timing of invasive angiography in high-risk NSTE-ACS patients remains uncertain.

Recommendations include randomizing low-risk patients to routine or selective invasive strategy and conducting RCTs testing different time intervals to perform angiography within the 72 h window after initial presentation.
Antithrombotic therapy: Whether pre-treatment with oral P2Y12 receptor inhibitors prior to ICA improves clinical outcomes in NSTE-ACS patients is uncertain.

Whether platelet function testing or genetic testing to guide de-escalation of oral P2Y12 receptor inhibitors after the first month of therapy following PCI improves clinical management and outcomes remains unclear.
The optimal long-term antithrombotic regimen in NSTE-ACS patients who have undergone PCI is unknown.
After stopping DAPT, a head-to-head comparison based on superiority between aspirin and alternative strategies is suggested (uncertain).
Recommended trials / actions: Randomize patients to pre-treatment with oral P2Y12 receptor inhibitors or no pre-treatment prior to ICA.
Randomize ACS patients to prasugrel or ticagrelor, both without pre-treatment.
Prospectively test a strategy based on platelet function testing or genetic testing in patients who may benefit from de-escalating antithrombotic therapy.
Conduct RCTs evaluating the benefit-risk balance for ischaemic versus bleeding events for different antithrombotic durations.
